1 Summary
2 Appellant entered into “short-sale” transactions in short-term securities that occurred over
3 six days in December of 1997. In effecting the transactions, appellant borrowed securities from his
4 stock broker, sold them, and contributed the proceeds to a partnership that he had recently formed. The
5 partnership assumed appellant’s obligation to return securities to the stockbroker in repayment of his
6 obligation. Appellant then contributed his interest in that partnership to a second partnership that he had
7 also recently formed. After the first partnership fulfilled its obligation to return the securities, the
8 second partnership withdrew from the first partnership, received other assets that appellant had
9 contributed to the first partnership, and sold them. The transactions in which the securities were sold,
10 replaced, and returned resulted in a small economic loss. However, the second partnership reported a
11 large loss with respect to the sale of the other assets on its tax return, offset that claimed loss against
12 capital gain from the sale of real property held by another partnership (a substantial interest in which
13 appellant had also contributed to the second partnership), and “passed through” the overall loss to
14 appellant. After auditing appellant and the partnerships, respondent disallowed the claimed loss from
15 the sale of the other assets on the ground that the basis in the other assets had been manipulated to be
16 inappropriately high, assessed additional tax, and imposed an accuracy-related penalty for the
17 underpayment of tax attributable to negligence. Respondent characterized the transactions at issue as a
18 variant of a “Son of Boss” tax shelter, which uses contrived steps with partnerships for the purpose of
19 generating artificial tax losses to offset income from other transactions.

22 Products (“Action”), for thirty-five years before 1997. Action was a subcontractor that sold highly

27 his own mistakes. Action is no longer in business, and appellant is living in another state.
